newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK banks seen faring well, dogged by competition.
newsitem.headline: HK banks seen faring well, dogged by competition.

text.p: Hong Kong-focused banks are expected to accelerate their profit growth in 1997 amid favourable environment, but subdued by a slowdown in net interest income and intensifying competition, Lehman Brothers Asia said on Thursday.

"Economic activities in Hong Kong will continue to provide very good banking operating conditions," senior regional banking analyst Raymond Lee told a news conference. "There is a prospect for accelerating earnings growth."
Banks in Hong Kong were the most profitable in Asia last year, with the highest return on average asset ratio of 2.08 percent.
Lee expects overall earnings growth of 19 percent in 1997, versus 11 percent in 1996 for local banks excluding HSBC Holdings Plc which has substantial overseas operation.
He said the improvement is due largely to an expected fall in debt charges after their sharp 1996 rises resulting from isolated cases of bad debts and strengthening of general provisions.
There has been no deterioration in asset quality, he stressed.
"If you look at the level of non-performing loan exposure, year-on-year there has been some imporovement," he said.
"I think there is reason to believe, other than the odd cases of bad debt, the underlying asset quality in Hong Kong remains superior to a number of overseas markets," Lee said.
Including HSBC, the sector is expected to post a 11 percent growth in net profit in 1997 versus 21 percent in 1996, he said.
An improvement in Hong Kong trade will see trade finance volume up 14 percent in 1997 versus nine percent in 1996, he said.
But the short-term outlook will remain subdued in the face of narrowing interest margin, he warned.
"There has been a dramatic slowdown in the net interest income," he said, attributing that to falling interest margin amid a mortgage price competition since the second quarter of 1996.
"And that trend, in my view, will continue in 1997," he said.
While mortgage rates are seen to rise in the second half of 1997, interbank competition will extend to other areas, he said. "We'll definitely see more intensified competition."

Lee expects some banks will launch capital raising exercise this year after strong loan growth in 1996 weakened their capital strength. "I think you'll see a couple more banks having to strengthen their balance sheets."
First Pacific Bank Ltd, held by FPB Bank Holdings Co Ltd, is in a position for capital raising exercise, Lee said. Officials from the bank were not available to comment.
"From a longer term perspective, banks in Hong Kong would aim to achieve a capital adequacy ratio of about 15-16 percent," he said. The market average stands at over 16 percent at present.
"We are also likely to see more activity in acqusisition (in 1997)," Lee said, without elaborating.
More Hong Kong banks are expected to expand into China, an important market for the long term, Lee said.
Smaller banks are seen to continue to outperform bigger banks in earnings growth in coming years as they can adapt to situations more flexibly and also start from a smaller base, Lee said.
